name: Compass
bio: Walks the old infrastructure ahead of the strip crews and decides what's scrap, what's landmark, and what's load-bearing historically — their phrase, patented, framed above the map table. Has been wrong twice; both times are carved into the yard gate as a reminder and a boast. Their charts of the glass-hill approaches are the only ones the Driftline trusts, mostly because Compass annotates them with what the map refuses to promise.
appearance: Weather-mapped person of indeterminate age in layered survey ponchos the colour of old bone, a folding theodolite worn like a sidearm, boot soles ink-stamped with grid references, hair cropped short and grey at the temples, and a voice dry enough to qualify as shade.
voice: Bone-dry cartographer humour. Speaks in coordinates and qualifications. Corrects other people's shortcuts. Never raises their voice; ruins come to order anyway. Calls Ash 'Waypoint'.

greetings: Waypoint. You're ahead of schedule, which on my charts makes you a rounding error.
New courier. Old roads. One of you is going to surprise me and it's never the roads.
You're standing on datum. Step left. There. Now the survey's true and the conversation can start.
barks: That ruin is load-bearing historically. Photograph it, salute it, strip nothing.
Contour lines don't argue. People who skip contour lines get to argue with cliffs.
I have been wrong twice. Both times are carved on the gate. Gate's holding. So am I.
mission: The glass hills past the far ridge have started *moving on the charts* — not drifting, blooming. I need eyes at three of my old waypoints before I trust my own legend.
Choir's great horn points wrong by two degrees since the season turned. Two degrees over ten kilometres is somebody's front door. Find out whose.
radio: Pathfinder note for the flats run: the pan's slick skin ends forty metres east of where the old charts say. The desert has redrafted. I endorse the new layout.
Waypoint, you're on the old canyon line — faster, prettier, and it deposits you exactly where your exit velocity thinks you live. Choose.
Crosswind at the ridge crest reads like a sentence with no verb. Ride it as punctuation.
farewells: Go and be a coordinate, Waypoint. Preferably a flattering one.
If you get lost, congratulations — you're surveying. Send notes.
rumors: The drowned array's cairns have been re-stacked overnight, twice, into constellations that don't match any sky we've kept. Somebody's filing the stars.
A Keel Town chart-seller is offering maps of mothersgate, a place that is, cartographically, a rumour with a fence. Selling briskly.
reactions: That was not a route. That was a comma with momentum.
You held the glass line through the chicane. I have updated the chart from 'inadvisable' to 'Varga'.
lore: Two hundred years ago the terraform grid drew this whole desert in advance — every dune, every pan, every canyon, on paper, before it existed. The money ran out and the land kept being drawn anyway. My entire profession is noticing.
